Package com.documentum.fc.common

Class DfcSecurityProviderManager

java.lang.Object
com.documentum.fc.common.DfcSecurityProviderManager
public final class DfcSecurityProviderManager extends Object
Central manager for cryptographic security provider selection in DFC.

FIPS mode is automatically enabled at startup when the environment variable FIPS_ENABLED=true is set. When FIPS mode is active, DFC will use the Bouncy Castle FIPS provider (BCFIPS) and attempts to register it from the classpath before any cryptographic operation. If the BCFIPS provider cannot be found or instantiated, an IllegalStateException is thrown — there is no silent fallback when FIPS mode is explicitly requested. When the variable is absent or set to any value other than "true" (case-insensitive), DFC uses the JDK default (Sun) security providers.

This class provides factory methods for all JCE/JCA objects that automatically route through the appropriate provider.

Since:
25.4

    • getKeyStore

      public KeyStore getKeyStore() throws KeyStoreException
      Creates a PKCS12 KeyStore instance.

      PKCS12 is the FIPS 140-3 approved keystore container format, using AES for key encryption and SHA for integrity protection via the JDK's own defaults. It is used in both FIPS and non-FIPS mode.

      In FIPS mode, BCFIPS is registered at priority 1 (see registerFipsProviderDirect()) and supplies its own PKCS12 engine, which falls back to legacy 3DES/SHA-1 instead of the JDK's modern AES/SHA-256 defaults. This method therefore explicitly requests the JDK's PROVIDER_SUNJSSE provider so its compliant PKCS12 implementation is used instead. In non-FIPS mode BCFIPS is never registered (see registerProvider()), so the default provider-less lookup is used unchanged.

      Returns:
      a PKCS12 KeyStore instance
      Throws:
      KeyStoreException - if PKCS12 is unavailable (indicates a JVM configuration problem)
